title: the stolen voice

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending, and the machines at Saduek Sak 24 send other people's shirts around a drum all night. Je Fah sits on the bench under the fan with her phone turned up, and Lek's own voice comes out of it selling foam.
Listen to this. Nine hundred baht a mattress, three provinces, and they used the good take — the one where you slowed down on the price.
I told them to keep it. A voice bought by the hour should work nights too.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She thumbs the phone screen dark and sets it face-down on the bench between them, then nods at the empty queue board.
turns.dialogue: The appraiser from the tower said she'd come see the ad contract. She won't come. They never come down here after dark.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She points past the dryers toward the soi mouth, then presses the change-machine key into Lek's palm and folds his fingers over it.
turns.dialogue: Go on past the rank, a bit further than the rank. The broker at the camp gate has a phone that records. He'll do it for a tea glass.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She lifts the washed letter off the folding table and holds it up to the fan, squinting at the ink that has run.
turns.dialogue: You look like a man running on someone else's battery. Sit. Rest a minute. This letter survived the drum — it can wait for you to read it.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She raps the biscuit tin with one knuckle, then tips her chin at the laundromat door where Bank has just walked in with his charger.
turns.dialogue: He didn't call first. Nobody calls first anymore. If I'd known he was coming I'd have turned the shop down a little.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She slides the circle envelope across the bench toward Lek and taps the name written on it.
turns.dialogue: Mae Tim's been moping. Her share circle lost a member — he just had his heart broken, and a broken heart stops paying. The envelope's short.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She leans in close over the word notebook, her ring light still glowing in her bag, and lowers her voice.
turns.dialogue: I have something to tell you. The mattress company wants a hundred more recordings. They'll pay per word. They'll pay for your name on the contract.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She flips the phone over and shows him the ad's view count, then lets it drop back onto the bench.
turns.dialogue: Everyone knows that voice now. Everyone in three provinces. You're famous and you didn't even have to leave the soi.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She shakes her head hard and pushes the deed bag back across the folding table toward him.
turns.dialogue: No. I don't agree with you. A voice that carries is a voice that should be used. You want to keep it quiet, you keep it in that notebook and nobody hears it.

je_fah_turn_1.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_1.line: She wipes the queue board clean with her sleeve. 'Write the appraiser's name on it anyway. If she comes, she comes.'

je_fah_turn_2.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_2.line: She tucks the tea glass into his hand along with the key. 'The broker drinks from it. It's how you know he's listening.'
je_fah_turn_2.bubble: Received: the change-machine key and the tea-stall glass

je_fah_turn_3.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_3.line: She smooths the washed letter flat on the folding table. 'There. Read it now, before the ink decides to leave.'

je_fah_turn_4.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_4.line: She slides the tin's lid open. Inside, three vendors' ledgers sit in order, and one thin notebook of words sits on top. 'You keep other people's books. Keep your own voice in one too.'

je_fah_turn_5.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_5.line: She counts the envelope twice and writes the shortfall on the back with her thumbnail. 'Mae Tim won't ask. That's the trouble with her.'

je_fah_turn_6.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_6.line: She taps the notebook's cover. 'Write your name in it. Then it's yours, whatever the app says.'

je_fah_turn_7.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_7.line: She laughs, but she looks at the view count longer than she looks at him. 'Famous. And still here, folding shirts.'

je_fah_turn_8.speaker: char_je_fah
je_fah_turn_8.line: She pushes the deed bag until it touches his hand. 'That's the paperwork nobody's written yet. A voice with a deed.'

finale.dialogue: She turns the shop back up, all the way, and the fan and the dryers and her phone make one loud room.
Lek's voice goes out of her phone again, selling foam to three provinces. In the notebook, his name sits on a page no one pays for, and the drum turns, and the quiet name waits.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: Pocket notebook, cover soft from handling, pages filled with other people's words in Lek's small hand — none of them paid for.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: Biscuit tin, lid bent from a decade of thumbs, three vendors' ledgers inside and a thin space left on top.

obj_score_report.name: the laminated score report
obj_score_report.description: Exam score report, laminated against the rain, three points short of the line, kept in his back pocket like a receipt.

obj_letter_washed.name: the washed letter
obj_letter_washed.description: A letter that went through the drum, ink run into blue ghosts, still folded the way it was mailed.

obj_deed_bag.name: the deed in the rice bag
obj_deed_bag.description: Land deed wrapped in a rice bag and tied with string, the paper soft at the corners from being carried.

obj_chalk_board.name: the queue board
obj_chalk_board.description: Chalk board by the change machine, names and slot times rubbed out and rewritten so often the slate has gone grey.

obj_share_envelope.name: the circle envelope
obj_share_envelope.description: Envelope with a share circle's payout inside, names on the front in Mae Tim's hand, one name crossed out.

obj_change_key.name: the change-machine key
obj_change_key.description: Small brass key on a red plastic tag, worn smooth, opens the change machine and nothing else.

obj_tea_glass.name: the tea-stall glass
obj_tea_glass.description: Small tea glass, rim chipped, the broker at the camp gate drinks from it while he listens.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She takes the notebook and writes his name on the first page in her big market hand. 'There. Now the app has to argue with paper.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Je Fah has written Lek's name in the notebook

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She lifts the tin's lid and lays the notebook inside, on top of the ledgers. 'Keep your voice where you keep the books. Then it's a record, not a rumor.' She presses the change-machine key into his hand.

char_je_fah: She turns the {item} over once and sets it back on the bench. 'Not that. Not yet.'
She taps the {item} against the folding table. 'A voice needs a name on paper before it needs anything else.'
She pushes the {item} back toward him. 'Write your name in the notebook first. Then we'll see about the tin.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the night with nothing settled. The drum turns; Je Fah's phone sells foam.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Je Fah watches the view count the way clerks watch clocks.
Je Fah's gaze flicks from the {item} to the notebook in Lek's pocket and back — a name unmade, a record unkept.
